solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The Mexican spread out taco dough first to form a thick covering

indicators.note: first says the dough comes at the front, ahead of the Spanish article

parts.note: duff is a dialect word for dough, as in plum duff
el is 'the' in Spanish, the language of Mexico

indicators.note: spread out says the four letters of taco are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Mexican cook stretches taco dough to make a thick blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel coat is a heavy woollen overcoat, a thick covering for the body.

clue.text: Argue about humble doctor sacked to make way for graduate

indicators.note: sacked to make way for says one piece is thrown out and another takes its place

parts.note: to humble someone is to demote them, lower their rank
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A dispute over a lowly doctor being fired so a graduate can have the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a matter is to discuss or argue about it.

clue.text: Notable Romeo arrested and facing trumped-up charges

indicators.note: arrested means held, so one word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: famed means notable, well known
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A well-known lover is arrested and faces false charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone framed has been set up, with evidence faked to incriminate them.

clue.text: Unable to attend church, old flame got in touch

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame
communicated means made contact, got in touch

explanation.surface: Kept from church, someone hears again from a former lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A person cut off from the church's communion is barred from taking part in its services.

clue.text: Dance till jiggered by romantic glow

indicators.note: jiggered means messed about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dancing until worn out in soft, romantic light.
explanation.definitionFit: A candlelit dinner is lit by candles, the classic soft and romantic illumination.

clue.text: 'Room At The Top' is at the core of narrative Fifties fiction and genuinely parochial

indicators.note: at the core of says to take the central letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A literary judgement that the novel Room at the Top is truly provincial Fifties fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Room at the Top is John Braine's 1957 novel of northern provincial life, so the surface reads as criticism; the title is really a cryptic description of a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room at the very top of a house, under the roof.

clue.text: Good articles about government can become unbalanced

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the next letter

parts.note: A and A are two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Fine newspaper pieces on the government can go off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is slang for mentally confused or senile, not in balance.

clue.text: Winning horse wrapping up finish before half mile

indicators.note: wrapping up means enclosing, so the horse goes round the next word

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
to do, as in do for, is to finish someone off

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the word mile

explanation.surface: A racing report: the winning horse is wrapping things up before the half-mile marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning in the sense of charming or endearing, as in a winning smile.

clue.text: Black Sabbath are not commonly without hot Ovaltine for the last drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters surround the next pair

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of are not
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the last picks out the final letter of Ovaltine

explanation.surface: Fans of the heavy metal band Black Sabbath shun a mug of cocoa-like Ovaltine for a final tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit, a type of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Newspaper editor on track to produce current layout

parts.note: print stands for the newspapers, the print media
a circuit is a racing track

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor gets on the right lines to produce the latest page layout.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed circuit is a board with conducting paths laid out for electric current.

clue.text: Occasionally bolt a snack in a sec?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so take every other letter starting with the first

explanation.surface: Wolfing down a snack now and then in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sec' looks like a second but is French for dry: blanc sec is dry white wine, so the word sits in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the French wine term blanc sec, meaning dry white, this word stands beside sec.

clue.text: It's well-known common sense takes over with riot erupting

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so common sense holds the other letters

parts.note: nous is common sense, gumption

indicators.note: erupting means bursting into disorder, so the letters of riot are scrambled

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Good sense is overwhelmed when a riot breaks out, as everyone knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous, usually for something bad; widely recognised.

clue.text: Warm weather Malta enjoys

indicators.note: enjoys says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holiday note that Malta has warm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal relates to heat, as in thermal underwear that keeps you warm.

clue.text: Kettle in action controversially before end of demonstration

indicators.note: controversially suggests something disputed and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
end of picks out the final letter of demonstration

explanation.surface: Police kettling protesters, a contentious tactic, before a demonstration ends.
explanation.walkthrough: To kettle is British police slang for penning protesters into a confined area.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettling protesters means hemming them in, keeping them confined in one place.

clue.text: General well-being resulting from the chill BUPA treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Good health comes from the private health insurer BUPA treating a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: BUPA is a British private healthcare company.
explanation.definitionFit: Public health is the health of the population as a whole, the community's welfare.

clue.text: Calm decor designed to be emollient

indicators.note: designed means arranged to a plan, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A soothing interior design scheme of calm decor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is a soothing skin cream, a moisturising softener for the skin.

clue.text: Toothless creatures displaying stomachs after a half-pint

indicators.note: after says the stomachs come behind the half-pint
half here takes the second half of the word pint, its last two letters

parts.note: to stomach something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: Creatures without teeth showing off their bellies after half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antbears, aardvarks or giant anteaters, eat ants and lack proper teeth.

clue.text: Oddly satire and adult entertainment first for high jump

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on
first picks out the opening letter of entertainment

explanation.surface: Satire and adult shows are oddly the warm-up for an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: The straddle is a high-jump technique, crossing the bar face down with legs astride.

clue.text: 'Tricky Belfast kid scores into empty net' — about time to reveal this description of Keegan

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters wrap round one more
tricky means wily or involved, so the letters are thoroughly mixed
empty means hollowed out, leaving only the outer letters of net

explanation.surface: A tricky Belfast lad slots the ball home, then a famous put-down of Kevin Keegan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Belfast kid is George Best; Stan Bowles (or Danny Blanchflower in some tellings) quipped that Kevin Keegan was not fit to lace Best's drinks, mocking the usual 'boots'.
explanation.definitionFit: The full quotation is the remark itself, a disparaging verdict comparing Keegan unfavourably with Best.

clue.text: Part of September I'm in Ibizan resort

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker spends part of September on Ibiza at a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is an Italian seaside town on the Adriatic, a well-known holiday destination.

clue.text: See 18
Sickness returns tucking into rum baba for din-dins perhaps

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the sickness is placed within the rearranged letters
rum means odd or strange, so the letters of baba are rearranged
returns means the word for sickness is read backwards

parts.note: mal is French for illness, as in mal de mer

explanation.surface: A queasy diner recovers enough to tuck into a rum baba for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nursery words: baby talk for a lamb, as din-dins is baby talk for dinner.

clue.text: See 18
Celebrity's first to get more pretentious make of watch

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of Celebrity

parts.note: artier means more arty, more affectedly cultured

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets showier by wearing a luxury watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartier is a French luxury brand known for its watches and jewellery.

clue.text: A comedian 'espousing' women's clothing — it's his delivery

indicators.note: espousing means embracing, so the comedian's name holds the clothing inside

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian
a dress is a woman's garment

explanation.surface: A comedian takes up cross-dressing, and that is how he performs his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like a comic's timing but means a parcel or letter delivered to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person a letter or parcel is sent to, so the delivery is theirs.

clue.text: Alliance exposed by small number in U-turn

indicators.note: turn says the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
the letter U from U-turn

explanation.surface: A coalition is revealed when a few members perform a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together, such as a federation or league of parties.

clue.text: Leak head of state's energy record

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of state

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: A leak exposes the head of state's record on energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To seep is to ooze or trickle slowly through, as liquid escaping from a container.

clue.text: Exercise regime several critics start off confused about

indicators.note: confused about means muddled and turned around, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: some means several, a few

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter of critics is removed

explanation.surface: Several critics are bewildered about a fitness programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometrics is a form of exercise where muscles are tensed against resistance without moving.
